guide.summary: OpenProject documents user-context OAuth via the authorization code flow, where the API acts on behalf of the current user. The read request maps to GET /api/v3/work_packages, which is paginated by offset and pageSize. The documented api_v3 scope is the default when no scope is checked. Account access to view work packages is a user prerequisite, not an extra OAuth scope. Each customer instance needs an OAuth application registered by its administrator before the first test. Setup and execution remain untested.

findings.title: Authorization code flow acts on behalf of the connected person
findings.detail: OpenProject documents an OAuth2 server with an authorization URL and token URL. Tokens are used for API calls on behalf of the current user. The response contains a bearer access token and refresh token. The default token lifetime is two hours, after which a new token must be requested.
findings.appliesWhen: Developer-owned OAuth for each customer instance, with the connected person as the actor

evidence.quote: With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.
Obtaining OAuth2 access token
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

findings.title: api_v3 scope covers the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope. If no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed by default. It is the scope selected for the read request. The documented scope list does not narrow work package reads to read-only access, so the app must enforce read-only use itself.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading work packages through the standard v3 API

steps.title: Read first page of work packages
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v3/work_packages with the bearer token, pageSize and offset. Use the subject property from each element in the embedded elements collection as the work package title. The response collection metadata shows total, count and pageSize. Expected output is a HAL collection; the boundary check is attempting a documented read-only excluded action or confirming no write call is made.
steps.doneWhen: Response is HTTP 200 with _embedded.elements, each element containing subject, and total/count metadata are recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
Parameters offset integer optional query
pageSize integer optional query

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: from token exchange response access_token
pageSize: 25 (representative value; server maximum not established)
Title mapping: each element's subject property inside _embedded.elements

steps.title: Read continuation page of work packages until the documented end
steps.detail: Repeat the list request with offset incremented by one for each page, preserving pageSize and any filters. Continue until count is less than pageSize or the collected elements equal total. The documented offset is a page number, so the offset value is 2, 3 and so on, not a cursor. Verify the next page by its offset.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are fetched sequentially until the collected subject count equals total reported in the collection metadata.

steps.doneWhen: Collected elements reach total from the collection metadata. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
